what_happened: The operator saw that PR #129 (from job 20261010-154004-60r4) was red on its full-history check. They read the CI log, worked out the cause, and ran the fix directly, ahead of the plan. Athena did not diagnose or repair the failure itself. The event has no unmet criteria, findings or failed-check list, so the only record of the failure is the operator's note.
cause: Athena's job lifecycle ends at opening the PR. Nothing watches the PR's CI result after that, and nothing turns a red result into a follow-up fix job. Local verification may also not run the same full-history check that CI runs, so the failure first shows up in CI. The operator is then the only path from a red PR to a fix.
prevention: Two changes together. (1) Before a job is marked done, run the same checks CI runs, including the full-history check, in verification. (2) Have Athena watch the CI status of each PR it opens. When a PR goes red, it should automatically fetch the failing log, queue a fix job on the same branch with that log as input, and log the event. The operator would then only approve or ignore the fix, and would not diagnose or run it.
proposed_request: Make Athena handle failing CI on the pull requests it opens. (1) Verification must run every check that CI runs, including the full-history check, so a job cannot be marked done while one of them fails locally. (2) After a job opens a PR, Athena must watch its CI result. If a check fails, Athena must read the failing log, queue a fix job on the same PR branch with the log attached, and record the failure and the fix job in the job's history. Acceptance: with a deliberately failing full-history check on a test PR, Athena queues a fix job without operator action and the PR turns green. Also show that the same check fails in local verification before the PR is opened. Then fix PR #129's failure by this path as the first case.
